verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents a first-party sandbox that limits what the agent process and its children can read, write, and reach on the network, using OS-level enforcement (Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS). That covers code, tool subprocesses, and network access. Worktree sessions add file-level isolation between parallel agents, but that is a separate feature and is not credited here. Missing for 10: configuration depth (allow-lists, default policy, opt-in vs default), coverage on Windows, and any independent or hands-on corroboration that the sandbox enforces as described.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can have the agent operate inside a sandbox when interacting with code, tools, and network resources
